topic: Template Class Specialization and SFINAE for Conditional Compilation
explanation: In C++, template specialization allows developers to define custom implementations of a template for specific types or conditions, enabling tailored behavior. Substitution Failure Is Not An Error (SFINAE) is a technique that leverages template specialization and overload resolution to enable or disable template instantiations based on compile-time conditions. Together, these features facilitate writing highly generic, efficient, and type-safe code that adapts to different types or traits without runtime overhead.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how template specialization combined with SFINAE enables conditional compilation of functions based on type traits. The IsIntegral template uses std::enable_if to selectively enable function overloads for integral and non-integral types. When 'process' is called with an integer, the integral version is instantiated and executed; for floating-point or string types, the non-integral version is selected. This approach allows writing flexible, type-safe code that adapts to different types at compile time without runtime overhead, exemplifying advanced template programming techniques in modern C++.
